history.origins: Tribello is a regional American trick-taking game from Illinois, USA. It was contributed by Mary Beale, whose family from DeKalb County have played it since the 1930s or 1940s. The game is a whist-type quota game with four distinct rounds (cut trump, dealer names trump, no trump, and nullo).
timeline: 1930s–1940s: Played by families in DeKalb County, Illinois; rules documented from family tradition.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Deal 4 hands of 13 (3 players + 1 pickup/widow).
setup.dealing: 13 cards each + 13-card pickup. Players exchange with pickup.

rules.objective: Highest total score after 12 deals (4 rounds x 3 deals).
rules.gameplay: Exchange with pickup. Play 13 tricks. Quotas: Dealer=6, Left=4, Right=3. Rounds: 1=Cut trump, 2=Dealer picks, 3=No trump, 4=Nullo (avoid tricks, reversed quotas).

strategy.basic: Exchange wisely with the pickup. Adjust play to round type.
strategy.intermediate: In Nullo, dump high cards early.
strategy.advanced: Calculate what opponents exchanged from the pickup.

scoring.description: +1 per trick above quota. -1 per trick below quota. Round 4: reversed.
scoring.winCondition: Highest total score after 12 deals (4 rounds x 3 deals).
